title: Large-scale vitreous fluid proteomics using 1D SDS-PAGE, tandem mass spectrometry, and a relational database
protocol: Solubilize samples in 2X sample buffer.
Heat samples at 96°C for 5 minutes.
Place samples on ice briefly until ready for use.
Centrifuge samples at 14000 rpm for 5 minutes in an Eppendorf centrifuge.
Normalize samples to undiluted vitreous volume (e.g., 50 μl).
Wash glass plates and all chambers thoroughly.
Prepare resolving gel (12%) containing components as specified.
Prepare stacking gel (4%) containing components as specified.
Load normalized samples onto SDS-PAGE.
Load samples and prestained molecular weight markers on the gel.
Carry out electrophoresis at a constant current of 30 mA per gel (1.5-mm-thick) for approximately 3-4 hours.
Reduce the current to 15 mA or 7 mA if running the gel overnight for improved resolution.
Turn off power supply and disconnect cables when the tracking dye reaches the bottom of the gel.
Submerge the gel in enough Coomassie Blue staining solution that it floats freely.
Shake the gel slowly on a laboratory shaker or rocker for 30-60 minutes.
Destain the gel with several changes of destaining solution until the background is transparent (gentle rocking for about 2-3 hours).
Acquire gel images using your chosen imaging system.
Store the gel in 7% acetic acid solution at 4°C for up to several weeks prior to in-gel digestion.
Divide the entire lane for each sample into 60-70 slices of 1 mm width.
Place the slices in eppendorf tubes.
Store the slices at -20°C for several weeks prior to in-gel digestion.
Add 1 ml of water to remove any residual acid.
Discard the water.
Add 1 ml of a 50% acetonitrile: 50% 50 mM ammonium bicarbonate and soak for 30 min to 1 h.
Remove 1 ml of a 50% acetonitrile: 50% 50 mM ammonium bicarbonate.
Add 200 μl of acetonitrile to completely dehydrate gel slices.
Let sit in acetonitrile for approximately 10 min and then remove acetonitrile.
Dry gel chips in the speed vac until completely dry.
Rehydrate slices by adding 90 μl trypsin digest solution and incubate overnight at 37°C.
Remove supernatant and save for analysis.
Rinse slice three times with 80% acetonitrile, 1% formic acid.
Remove liquid and pool with supernatant from step 14.
Dry down digest in Speed Vac until approximately 2 μl remains.
Resuspend in 18 μl 2% Acetonitrile.
Separate the samples with microcapillary reverse-phase column in line with a LTQ linear ion trap mass spectrometer.
Prepare a protein database in FASTA format from NCBI or EBI.
Index the Database with Database Manager.
Set indexer parameters to Monoisotopic Trypsin (KR), fully enzymatic, MW range 300-3500, missed cleavage sites 0, differential/PTM M+16 and C+71.
Process multiple .raw files through TurboSEQUEST using an MW Range of 600-3500 and a Threshold of Absolute, 5000.
Set Precursor ion tolerance to 1.4 Mass Units: AMU.
Group Scan with a Minimum group count of 1 and Minimum ion count of 15.
Use Auto for Charge State and MSn level.
Export TurboSEQUEST search results into XML, excel or SQT format.
Enter resultant matches into a MySQL relational database.

Remove low-scoring peptides that do not meet the criteria: Cross-correlation score > 1.5, 2.0, and 2.5 for charge states +1, +2, and +3; Delta Correlation > 0.1; Primary Score > 200; Ranking of the Primary Score < 3; and percent fragment ions > 30%.
Proceed with peptide level filtering.
Summarize the filtered data.
Perform protein level filtering.
Report the final results.
Combine all search results from a sample generated from an entire lane of gel slices into a single file based on the protein accession number.
Retain slice number information in this file for later filtering and analysis.
Filter redundant proteins, trypsin, keratin, and proteins that do not have 2 unique peptides identified from a single slice or adjacent slices.
Compile all samples into one file.

If multiple accession numbers are assigned for a peptide match, select uniform accession numbers consistent with all peptide matches for that protein to enable comparison of proteins identified from different samples.
